questions.text:
Which of the following is/are correct inorder traversal sequence(s) of binary search tree(s)?
I. 3, 5, 7, 8, 15, 19, 25
II. 5, 8, 9, 12, 10, 15, 25
III. 2, 7, 10, 8, 14, 16, 20
IV. 4, 6, 7, 9 18, 20, 25
questions.solution:
In-order traversal of a BST is always sorted.

- I: sorted [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] valid
- II: 12 before 10 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] invalid
- III: 10 before 8 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] invalid
- IV: sorted [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] valid

Answer: I and IV only

questions.text: Which one of the following is TRUE at any valid state in shift-reduce parsing?
questions.solution:
In a valid shift-reduce parse, the stack content is always a viable prefix, i.e. a prefix of some right sentential form that does not go past the handle.

Answer: The stack contains only a set of viable prefixes

questions.text: Which one of the following is NOT equivalent to [latex]p\leftrightarrow q[/latex]?
questions.solution:
[latex]p\leftrightarrow q[/latex] is true when p and q are equal.

- Options 1, 2: [latex](p\rightarrow q)\wedge(q\rightarrow p)[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] equivalent
- Option 4: both false or both true [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] equivalent
- Option 3: exactly one is true, which is XOR, the negation of [latex]p\leftrightarrow q[/latex]

Answer: [latex](\neg p\wedge q)\vee(p\wedge\neg q)[/latex]

questions.text:
For a set A, the power set of A is denoted by [latex]2^{A}[/latex]. If A={5,{6},{7}}, which of the following options are TRUE?
I. [latex]\phi \in 2^{A}[/latex]
II. [latex]\phi \subseteq 2^{A}[/latex]
III. {5,{6}} [latex]\in 2^{A}[/latex]
IV. {5,{6}}[latex]\subseteq 2^{A}[/latex]
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: [latex]\phi\subseteq A[/latex], so [latex]\phi\in2^A[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- II: the empty set is a subset of every set [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- III: {5, {6}} [latex]\subseteq[/latex] A, so it is an element of [latex]2^A[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- IV: would need 5 [latex]\in2^A[/latex], but 5 is not a subset of A [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False

Answer: I, II and III only
